title: CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, AXONAL, TYPE 2A1
alt_titles: CHARCOT-MARIE-TOOTH DISEASE, AXONAL, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT, TYPE 2A1
HEREDITARY MOTOR AND SENSORY NEUROPATHY IIA1

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene.

checks.claim: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A1 (CMT2A1) is caused by mutation in the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a loss-of-function KIF1B mutation in CMT2A patients, and its title says CMT2A is caused by a KIF1Bbeta mutation. CMT2A1 is OMIM's current name for the KIF1B-linked form of CMT2A.

paragraphs.text: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2) is an inherited peripheral neuropathy with variable age of onset and normal or slightly reduced nerve conduction velocity. It is distinct from CMT1 both pathologically and genetically (Ben Othmane et al., 1993). CMT2A1 is the form of autosomal dominant CMT2 that maps to the distal short arm of chromosome 1.

checks.evidence_quote: Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease type 2 (CMT2) is an inherited peripheral neuropathy

checks.evidence_quote: Localization of a gene (CMT2A) for autosomal dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 to chromosome 1p
checks.explanation: The paper localizes CMT2A to distal 1p. CMT2A1 is the later name for the same form.

paragraphs.text: Saito et al. (1997) described the clinical features of CMT2A in 2 Japanese families. The posterior and anterior tibial muscles were equally weak. Tendon reflexes were preserved in the upper limbs and reduced or absent in the lower limbs. The peripheral nerves were not enlarged. Only 20% of affected individuals had mild sensory disturbance.

paragraphs.text: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) studied 6 large CMT2 families in which the disorder showed autosomal dominant inheritance. Hentati et al. (1992) also described CMT2 as autosomal dominant.

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) studied 6 large CMT2 families.
checks.evidence_quote: We have performed pedigree linkage analysis in six large autosomal dominant CMT2 families
checks.explanation: The abstract states that six large CMT2 families were studied.

checks.claim: In the 6 large CMT2 families studied by Ben Othmane et al. (1993), CMT2 showed autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We have performed pedigree linkage analysis in six large autosomal dominant CMT2 families
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the families as autosomal dominant.

checks.claim: Hentati et al. (1992) described CMT2 as an autosomal dominant disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The autosomal dominant forms of hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies include the hypertrophic form (CMT1) and the neuronal form of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2).
checks.explanation: The abstract names CMT2 as one of the autosomal dominant forms of hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy.

paragraphs.text: Hentati et al. (1992) studied 2 CMT2 pedigrees and excluded the CMT2 locus from the region of chromosome 17 where CMT1A maps (lod score -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58). In a CMT1 pedigree analyzed alongside these families, they confirmed linkage to CMT1A (lod +3.67 at theta = 0.00). The CMT2 families also gave negative lod scores for the chromosome 1 region containing CMT1B (lod -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61).

checks.evidence_quote: Studying one CMT1 and two CMT2 pedigrees
checks.explanation: The paper states that it studied 2 CMT2 pedigrees.

checks.claim: In 2 CMT2 pedigrees, Hentati et al. (1992) excluded the CMT2 locus from the region of chromosome 17 where CMT1A maps, with a lod score of -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58.
checks.evidence_quote: we were able to exclude the CMT2 disease locus from the region of chromosome 17 (Z = -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58) where the CMT1A gene maps
checks.explanation: The exclusion and the lod score of -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58 match the paper.

checks.claim: In a CMT1 pedigree analyzed alongside the CMT2 families, Hentati et al. (1992) confirmed linkage to CMT1A with a lod score of +3.67 at theta = 0.00.
checks.evidence_quote: Studying one CMT1 and two CMT2 pedigrees, we were able to exclude the CMT2 disease locus from the region of chromosome 17 (Z = -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58) where the CMT1A gene maps (Z = +3.67 at theta = 0.00).
checks.explanation: The lod of +3.67 at theta = 0.00 for the CMT1A region in the CMT1 pedigree is stated. The abstract implies, but does not spell out, that this score came from the CMT1 pedigree.

checks.claim: The 2 CMT2 families studied by Hentati et al. (1992) gave negative lod scores for the chromosome 1 region containing CMT1B, with a lod score of -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61.
checks.evidence_quote: Similarly, negative lod score values were obtained in CMT2 for the region of chromosome 1 where the CMT1B gene has been located (Z = -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61).
checks.explanation: The negative lod score of -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61 matches the paper.

paragraphs.text: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) performed linkage analysis in 6 large autosomal dominant CMT2 families. They showed linkage to the microsatellite markers D1S160, D1S170, D1S244, D1S228, and D1S199 in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1. Multipoint analysis of the linked families placed the CMT2A gene most likely in the interval flanked by D1S244 and D1S228. The odds that the gene lay inside rather than outside this interval were approximately 70:1.

paragraphs.text: Saito et al. (1997) performed linkage analysis in 2 Japanese families with CMT2. The highest cumulative multipoint lod score was 3.69 at marker D1S244, consistent with linkage to the CMT2A locus on chromosome 1p35-p36.

checks.evidence_quote: we performed linkage analysis of two Japanese CMT2 families using markers flanking the CMT2A, CMT2B, and CMT2D loci

checks.claim: In 2 Japanese CMT2 families, Saito et al. (1997) obtained a highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 at marker D1S244.
checks.evidence_quote: The highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 was obtained at D1S244.
checks.explanation: The lod score and marker match the abstract.

checks.claim: The linkage results of Saito et al. (1997) in 2 Japanese CMT2 families were consistent with linkage to the CMT2A locus on chromosome 1p35-p36.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage mapping of the gene for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 to chromosome 1p (CMT2A)
checks.explanation: The title reports mapping to chromosome 1p (CMT2A), and the abstract places the CMT2A locus at 1p35-36.

paragraphs.text: Hentati et al. (1992) concluded that the hypertrophic (CMT1) and neuronal (CMT2) forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease are genetically heterogeneous. The CMT2 gene was not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped at that time.

checks.claim: Hentati et al. (1992) concluded that the hypertrophic (CMT1) and neuronal (CMT2) forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease are genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: The present study therefore provides evidence for genetic heterogeneity between the hypertrophic and the neuronal forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
checks.explanation: The paper states this conclusion directly.

checks.claim: Hentati et al. (1992) found that the CMT2 gene was not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped at that time.
checks.evidence_quote: demonstrates that the CMT2 gene is not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped to date.

paragraphs.text: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) used admixture analysis of two-point lod scores, supported by multipoint admixture analysis, and found significant evidence for genetic heterogeneity among their 6 CMT2 families. Three families (DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523) had posterior probabilities of 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88, respectively, of being of the linked type. The authors suggested that at least 2 different genes cause the CMT2 phenotype.

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) used admixture analysis of two-point lod scores, supported by multipoint admixture analysis, in their 6 CMT2 families.
checks.evidence_quote: Significant evidence for heterogeneity was found using admixture analysis and the two-point lod scores. Admixture analyses using the multipoint results for the markers D1S244, D1S228, and D1S199 supported the two-point findings.

checks.claim: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) found significant evidence for genetic heterogeneity among their 6 CMT2 families.
checks.evidence_quote: Significant evidence for heterogeneity was found using admixture analysis and the two-point lod scores.

checks.claim: CMT2 families DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523 had posterior probabilities of 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88, respectively, of being of the chromosome 1p-linked type.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families, DUK662, DUK1241, and 1523 gave posterior probabilities of 1.0, 0.98, and 0.88 of being of the linked type.
checks.explanation: The linkage in the paper is to 1p, so the 'linked type' is the 1p-linked type.

checks.evidence_quote: These findings suggest that the CMT2 phenotype is secondary to at least two different genes

paragraphs.text: Zhao et al. (2001) found a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene in patients with CMT2A, a disorder previously mapped to an interval containing KIF1B. KIF1B is a kinesin superfamily motor protein that had previously been shown to transport mitochondria. Zhao et al. (2001) described KIF1B-beta, an isoform that differs from KIF1B in its cargo-binding domain. They concluded that defects in axonal transport caused by a mutated motor protein can underlie human peripheral neuropathy.

checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.

checks.claim: The KIF1B mutation found by Zhao et al. (2001) in CMT2A patients is located in the motor domain.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that CMT2A patients contain a loss-of-function mutation in the motor domain of the KIF1B gene.

checks.claim: CMT2A had previously been mapped to an interval containing the KIF1B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A was previously mapped to an interval containing KIF1B.

checks.evidence_quote: This is clear indication that defects in axonal transport due to a mutated motor protein can underlie human peripheral neuropathy.

paragraphs.text: Zhao et al. (2001) reported that Kif1b knockout mice died at birth from apnea caused by nervous system defects. Knockout neurons that were dying in culture could be rescued by expressing the KIF1B-beta isoform. Heterozygous mice had a defect in the transport of synaptic vesicle precursors and developed progressive muscle weakness similar to that seen in human neuropathies.
